newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN'S QUEST FOR FOURTH WORLD TITLE BEGINS WELL.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN'S QUEST FOR FOURTH WORLD TITLE BEGINS WELL.

text.p: Reigning 500cc champion Michael Doohan of Australia launched his bid for a fourth world title by winning the Malaysian motorcycling grand prix on Sunday.
Doohan, riding a Honda, beat second-placed Alex Criville of Spain, also a Honda rider, by more than 11 seconds in the opening race of the year.
Third-placed Nobuatsu Aoki of Japan finished more than 13 seconds after the Australian.
Doohan set a lap record of one minute 24.840 seconds for the race at the 3.505-km Shah Alam track. The previous record of 1:25.100 was set by American John Kocinski in 1991.
Doohan, starting second after Japanese pole position holder Tadayuki Okada, stormed to the front on the fourth lap of the 33-lap, 155.665 km race and led for the rest of the way.
Okada finished 10th after falling behind on the third lap.
Criville, fourth on the starting grid, was locked in a neck-and-neck battle with Aoki, who started in third position.
Doohan said he had a tough start and was anxious about the rain in the early stages of the race.
"It was pretty hectic at the beginning and I was a little worried about the rain," said the 31-year-old Australian. "I had a game plan but what turned out wasn't the game plan.
"So I just tried to get out in front and get some clean air. The tyres were flawless so I didn't have to do much spinning and the machine was working really well," he added.
Doohan, however, said he was not too optimistic about next week's race in Suzuka, Japan.
"Japan is not entirely one of my favourite race tracks and the Japanese are very hard to beat in Japan. I'd be happy to finish (in the) top three," he said.

The triple winner in Malaysia said it was too early to forecast his chances for a fourth world title in 1997. Italian Giacomo Agostini and Briton Mike Hailwood are the only riders in history to have won the 500cc title four times in a row.
"One race is a long way to think about a championship. When we get to the part when we have a comfortable lead, then I'll be more certain," Doohan said.
Criville described his second place as a good beginning for the season while Aoki complained about tyre problems.
